messages:
eli: Heads-up — after the kernel-selector change (commit 4b9f7) I'm seeing a ~25% p95 latency regression on paged-attention for FlashV3 runs. Microbench here: /tmp/bench_flashv3.log

maria: Ugh. Is this on dedicated or hosted infra? Any obvious KV cache thrash?

eli: Dedicated. KV residency looks fine overall but the allocator pattern changed: chunked allocations are spiking; allocator churn -> small device memcpy stalls. Quick excerpt from the perf trace:

```
# flame summary (hot funcs)
flashv3_forward -> paged_attn_dispatch
paged_attn_dispatch -> slot_chunk_alloc
slot_chunk_alloc -> gpu_memset (heavy)
kv_page_fault_handler -> slot_chunk_alloc
```

sasha: Do we have a run id? can you paste the bench command you used?

eli: repro command: `./infra/bench --model flashv3 --seq 2048 --batch 8 --mode paged --kernel auto`
logs: /tmp/bench_flashv3.log (p95 went from 320ms -> 405ms after selector flip)

taylor: Sounds like the selector is preferring fused-flash variants that assume a denser KV layout, which forces slot_chunk_alloc to create lots of medium-sized ranges. We forgot to gate kernel choice on average kv-page-fill.

lina: Quick experiment: can you try forcing kernel back to flashv2? `--kernel flashv2` or set env `RW_KERNEL_PREF=flashv2`

eli: Tried flashv2 -> p95 goes back down to ~315ms. So kernel choice is the trigger. But not sure why chunk allocator gets hot. My hunch: sticky kernel assignment + batching heuristic leads to uneven per-worker KV residency skew, which trips the slot-chunk growth path.

maria: If it's sticky assignment, we might be keeping a less ideal kernel for long-lived streams. We should evaluate a short-lived re-eval window for kernel selection (e.g., re-eval every N = 8 requests or on big sequence length jumps).

sasha: Agreed. Also, try lowering `kv_pin_fraction` to 0.1 in the runtime config for a test — that reduces eager pinning and might avoid chunk splits.

eli: Re-ran with `kv_pin_fraction=0.1` and `--kernel auto` — p95 dropped to 335ms. Good improvement but still ~5% worse than v2.

taylor: Can you share the allocator stats? even counts and average chunk size would help.

eli: allocator dump (trimmed):
```
slot_chunk: total_allocs=1_203_456, avg_size=24KB, splits=12_345, merges=432
slab_pool: total_allocs=89_123, avg_size=512B
kv_pages: pinned=14%, resident=72%, swapped=14%
```

lina: Those splits look high for avg_size 24KB. The selector probably picks a kernel that requires contiguous ranges for vectorized kv loads, so allocator tries to coalesce, causing memcpy.

maria: Two quick mitigation ideas: (1) lower sticky interval so kernel re-eval happens earlier, (2) add a kernel fastpath that prefers a kernel variant tolerant of fragmented KV (even if slightly slower per-token, it avoids allocator churn).

eli: Agreed. I'll prototype (1) first — new flag RW_KERNEL_STICKY=8 -> re-eval after 8 requests. If that fails, follow up on (2).

sasha: Also file a telemetry event for every kernel decision with these fields: `model, kernel_variant, kv_fill_pct, mean_chunk_size, batch_size`. We need data to correlate.

maria: I'll add a small perf test that simulates workload skew (half long seqs, half short) to surface this. Put it under infra/bench/kv_skew_test.

eli: Quick heads-up: I pushed a branch `fix/kernel-sticky-quick` that sets sticky to 8 by default in our canary image. Rolling to canary now.

pagerbot: deploybot: roll started for canary group "kern-sticky-quick" (image: fix/kernel-sticky-quick). CI: passed. ETA 6m. :white_check_mark:

taylor: If canary looks good with flashv3 workloads then we can consider rolling to dedicated. Also add a smoke that runs bench with `--kernel auto` vs `--kernel flashv2` and fails if p95 regresses >10%.

eli: Canary logs show p95 back to ~320ms after roll. Will run extended sweep for 30m.

lina: Follow-up issue for runtime: revisit the slot_chunk_alloc growth heuristics — consider a split threshold combined with async copy to avoid blocking critical path.

maria: Filed infra ticket INFRA-1298 for the bench and telemetry changes. Runtime ticket RUNTIME-2143 for sticky re-eval + allocator heuristics.

eli: Nice work. Next steps: monitor canary telemetry (kernel_decisions, allocator_splits), evaluate if fastpath kernel variant needed. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
